asOf: Historical observation dates stated per event
note: Original Orbis factual annotations checked 14 October 2026; event-card links and scene-indexed notes identify the evidence. Points locate selected places approximately, not military fronts, camp boundaries or casualty-density surfaces. Contemporary coastlines are reference geography; modern country borders are hidden unless a scene explicitly compares country status. No comprehensive monthly occupation map is claimed.

items.title: Europe: January1938
items.text: CShapes records state boundaries on 1 January 1938. Austria and Czechoslovakia still appear separately. This is diplomatic geography before the year’s annexations, not a map of the eve of war in September 1939.

items.title: Vienna
items.text: German troops entered Austria on 12 March 1938; the Anschluss law incorporated it into Nazi Germany the following day. Vienna locates the annexation. No new territorial polygon is inferred from this point.

items.title: Munich
items.text: The agreement reached at Munich on 29–30 September 1938 allowed German annexation of the Sudetenland. The city point locates the negotiations; it does not draw the affected border districts.

items.title: Moscow
items.text: Germany and the Soviet Union signed their non-aggression pact on 23 August 1939. Its secret protocol divided spheres in eastern Europe and provided for Poland’s partition. The Moscow point locates the agreement, not its territorial clauses.
